_readme: Author aliases: how two spellings of one person become one node in the
Keys and values are the graph's internal author keys: surname + '|' + initials,
lower-cased with spaces and full stops removed. Every entry means 'the person
on the left is the person on the right'.
Two things produce duplicates, and both are in the source data rather than in
the code: the same person written in Persian on a Persian paper and in Latin on
an English one, and the same person written two ways in Latin ('Golaghaei
Darzi, A.' one year, 'Darzi, A.G.' another).
Run `node tools/check-authors.mjs` to see who is still unmerged. It lists
near-duplicates it can spot; it deliberately does not guess, because merging
two people who merely share a surname would be a lie about the work.
Nothing here is required. With this file missing or empty the graph still
builds; it just shows some people twice.
_persian_to_latin: the same collaborator, written in each script
_latin_variants: the same collaborator, written two ways in Latin
